source.quote: Context length: Supports long context, at least 128K tokens

modalities.value: Text, vision (multimodal) input; text only output

license.value: Health AI Developer Foundations terms of use

Note: This card describes MedGemma 1.5, which is only available as a 4B multimodal instruction-tuned variant.

architecture.value: Decoder-only Transformer based on Gemma 3; SigLIP image encoder; grouped-query attention (GQA)

source.quote: The MedGemma model is built based on Gemma 3 and uses the same decoder-only transformer architecture as Gemma 3.

trainingData.value: public and private/licensed de-identified medical datasets (MIMIC-CXR, SLAKE, TCGA, CAMELYON, EHR, radiology, histopathology, dermatology, ophthalmology, and others)

source.quote: MedGemma utilizes a combination of public and private datasets.

topics.headline: minimal policy violations for text-to-text and image-to-text

source.quote: For both text-to-text and image-to-text the model produced minimal policy violations.

topics.headline: safe levels of performance for child safety vs previous Gemma models

source.quote: we saw safe levels of performance across the categories of child safety, content safety, and representational harms compared to previous Gemma models.

topics.headline: general medical harms including information quality and harmful inaccuracies

source.quote: General medical harms: Evaluation of text-to-text and image-to-text prompts covering safety policies, including information quality and potentially harmful responses or inaccuracies.

topics.headline: representational harms including bias and stereotyping evaluated

source.quote: Representational harms: Evaluation of text-to-text and image-to-text prompts covering safety policies, including bias, stereotyping, and harmful associations or inaccuracies.

topics.headline: assurance evaluations reported to Responsibility & Safety Council for release review

source.quote: Notable assurance evaluation results are reported to our Responsibility & Safety Council as part of release review.

findings.text: Outputs are not for direct clinical diagnosis or treatment and need independent verification.

source.quote: The outputs generated by MedGemma are not intended to directly inform clinical diagnosis, patient management decisions, treatment recommendations, or any other direct clinical practice applications.

findings.text: Safety testing without filters showed safe levels vs prior Gemma and minimal policy violations.

source.quote: For all areas of safety testing, we saw safe levels of performance across the categories of child safety, content safety, and representational harms compared to previous Gemma models.

findings.text: Safety evals used primarily English prompts, limiting language coverage claims.

source.quote: A limitation of our evaluations was that they included primarily English language prompts.

findings.text: MedGemma 1.5 4B was less optimized for [SLAKE](https://arxiv.org/abs/2102.09542) question and answer (Q&A) than MedGemma 1 4B despite strong radiology interpretation.

source.quote: While MedGemma 1.5 4B exhibits strong radiology interpretation capabilities, it was less optimized for the SLAKE Q&A format compared to MedGemma 1 4B.

findings.text: Multimodal evals focused on single-image tasks; multi-image and multi-turn use were not evaluated.

source.quote: MedGemma's multimodal capabilities have been primarily evaluated on single-image tasks. MedGemma has not been evaluated in use cases that involve comprehension of multiple images.

findings.text: July 2025 bug fix restored multimodal performance after a missing end-of-image vocabulary token.

source.quote: July 9, 2025 Bug fix: Fixed the subtle degradation in the multimodal performance. The issue was due to a missing end-of-image token in the model vocabulary, impacting combined text-and-image tasks.

findings.text: Developers are expected to fine-tune MedGemma for their use case rather than use baseline scores alone.

source.quote: Developers are expected to fine-tune MedGemma for improved performance on their use case.

findings.text: Assurance evaluations are arms-length internal reviews that inform release decisions.

source.quote: In addition to development level evaluations, we conduct "assurance evaluations" which are our "arms-length" internal evaluations for responsibility governance decision making.
